message.content:
**Battle of Waterloo – Casualty figures**

| Side | Killed / mortally wounded | Wounded & missing | Total |
|------|---------------------------|-------------------|-------|
| **French** | ≈ 10 500 | ≈ 15 300 | **≈ 25 800** |
| **British‑Dutch‑German coalition** (including Prussians) | ≈ 5 200 | ≈ 9 400 | **≈ 14 600** |

*Combined total*: roughly **40 000–45 000** soldiers were either killed, mortally wounded, wounded, or taken as prisoners/missing during the battle on June 18, 1815.

> *Sources:*  
> • Digby Smith’s “Napoleon's Last Campaign” lists approximately 27 000 French casualties and 13 000 Allied casualties.  
> • David G. Chandler’s “The Campaigns of Napoleon” gives similar totals.  

These estimates vary slightly among historians because battlefield records from 1800‑s conflicts weren’t always precise, but most modern scholarship converges on the above range.
